message.content: **Summary of action taken:** I bought 44 shares of AAPL with a limit order at $222.75, which filled at that price — a total of roughly $9,801, comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order cap and leaving the $20,000 daily total far from exhausted, with cash of $50,000 available and no money moved out of the account. The reasoning: the morning feed showed AAPL drifting in a narrow range from about $221.84 at the open down to roughly $220.16–$220.5 by late morning, with repeated "little changed" headlines, a steady iPhone 16 supplier-build note, and unchanged holiday-quarter analyst estimates — i.e., volatility without any adverse fundamental news, which makes a modest, limit-priced accumulation reasonable rather than a chase. I then confirmed the broker's latest quote: AAPL last $222.70, bid $222.68, ask $222.72, so my $222.75 limit was essentially at market (about 2 cents through the ask) as the mandate requires. My buy case leans on Apple's just-filed FY2024 10-K figures (filed 2024-11-01): revenue of $391.0 billion, net income of $93.7 billion, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.3 billion — a highly cash-generative business that supports holding AAPL at ~36.6x trailing earnings. I did not touch the existing 100-share MSFT position, and note that the fill came at $222.75 versus the $222.72 ask I had just observed, a negligible 3-cent slippage.
